<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of one tiny island, in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  She idles. Every so often, something happens. Above: the same idea in 80 by 50 character cells.<br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut falls on a hermit crab, then walks off with the crab inside. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p and 30 fps, always daytime.

[activities.toml](activities.toml) holds more than 90 activities, most of them on four timers that go off anywhere from every 2 to 5 minutes (everyday routines) to every 3 to 6 hours (the super-rare ones). Each one waits for the next bar of the music (3 seconds), so every gag lands on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loop libraries, no recordings.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<sub>Live preview in the browser, then export a frame-exact, YouTube-ready MP4: the page encodes the frames and the server mixes in the sound. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.</sub>

<details>
<summary><b>PART ONE, PART TWO</b>: how the banner works, and why it cuts to a tunnel</summary>
<br>

The banner is a text-mode demo screen: VGA text at 80 columns by 50 rows, 9 by 8 dots a cell, 16 colours, and the rules the text-mode demo competitions kept. One character per cell, one foreground and one background colour, one fixed font, no palette tricks. Every in-between colour is a shade character laid over a background, which is why the sea comes in bands and the bands crawl.

None of the effects is ever redrawn. The sea, the lagoon, the sky, the sun and the tunnel are phase maps, worked out once by the generator, one number per cell. Every cell of an effect runs the same colour ramp (for the sea: blue, then cyan, then a light crest, and back), and each number starts one step further along it. That is palette cycling, done with nothing but a CSS animation delay: the swells roll in and the rings spread out from the island while every cell stays exactly where it is. The shade characters cycle too: each cell is drawn as four sets of dots, the sets that light, medium and dark shade are built from, and each set has its own colour track.

**Part two.** Once a minute, for two bars, the screen hard-cuts to a checkered tunnel and a super-rare event. In the video, *she could leave any time*: she walks out over the water, the island sits empty, and she comes back with an iced coffee. It is one of the super-rare events, which share a timer that goes off every 3 to 6 hours, and it happens at most once in ten hours. The banner shows it every minute, for convenience, and cuts back to her standing there with the coffee. Earlier, at 0:24, a message in a bottle goes out to the left, lands, and washes straight back to her feet, one cell per beat.

| The text-mode rules | The island's rules |
| --- | --- |
| 80 columns by 50 rows, nothing drawn between the cells | one stationary frame, 16:9, 1080p at 30 fps |
| 16 colours; anything else is a shade character | always daytime |
| one fixed font, no palette tricks | no samples: every sound is synthesized from code |
| effects step from cell to cell | hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults |
| the scroller moves one character at a time | every gag waits for the next bar of the music |
| judged on what happens on screen | almost nothing happens, on purpose |

With reduced motion switched on, the banner holds its opening frame: the sea mid-swell, the coffee in her hand, the scroller at the start.

The style is credited to the Text Mode Demo Contest (run by tAAt from 1996, continued by Northern Dragons up to 2017). Nothing from any demo is copied here: the block letters, the 8x8 font (an original stand-in for the PC's own), the effects and the island were drawn for this banner by its generator. Crawlspace and the Horse Latitudes text mode compo are made up.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>EVERY SO OFTEN</b>: the timers, the gags and the scene</summary>
<br>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) lists more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-02, and more arrive every few hours). Most sit on four timers; the rest are chained follow-ups that only ever start as the sequel to another activity.

| Timer | Goes off every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 per run | about 2 |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs; chained follow-ups come on top. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea can be busy while she is. The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`; `python tools/schedule.py` validates the file and simulates one.

```text
 ── SCENE LIST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  · a message in a bottle washes straight back. later, a different
    bottle brings a reply
  · a delivery drone drops a parcel: another pair of headphones
  · a sea turtle visits. a shark in headphones nods to the beat
  · a stray cat (grey tabby, white chest) arrives on a crate, climbs the
    palm and naps. one day it floats away again. another day, it's back
  · the signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the very top of the palm
  · a coconut falls on a hermit crab. the coconut walks off, crab inside
  · a tour boat of selfie-takers. a bro on an electric hydrofoil throws
    a shaka and carves off
  · she could leave any time: out over the water, back with an iced coffee
  · bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear
    fishing. a kumara she plants grows over the course of the video
  · coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue, and a
    sandcastle, which the tide takes

 ── THE SCENE, WITHOUT HER ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  26 entries: 4 always-on effects, 22 timed events. built: waves on the
  shore and cloud shadows drifting over the sea. planned: distant birds,
  planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers,
  a gecko and a rain shower (daytime rain; it is always daytime)
```

</details>

<br>

```text
 ── THE TOOLS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  python tools/serve.py ............ the renderer: live preview at
                                     http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and an export
                                     to a YouTube-ready MP4
  python tools/schedule.py ......... validate the schedule, simulate a
                                     ten-hour run
  python tools/make_audio.py ....... synthesize every sound from code
  python tools/render_demo.py --dev  a dev reel of every activity with a
                                     heads-up display (the older Python
                                     reference renderer)

  the export is frame-exact H.264 made in the browser (WebCodecs, 68 to 78
  frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome); the server mixes the sound and
  joins the two into an MP4

 ── THE SOUND ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  more than 150 sound files, every one synthesized from code
  theme ....... a seamless 60 s loop at 80 BPM in F major, ii-V-I-vi,
                20 bars of exactly 3 s: electric piano, kalimba lead,
                soft drums, vinyl crackle
  ocean ....... also a seamless 60 s loop
  levels ...... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, adjustable in
                master and per routine
  heard by .... nobody yet. measured to the decibel, in total silence

 ── GREETZ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  crawlspace greets the ninth dot preservation league · the ramp rotary
  club · the phase map cartographers · the medium shade society · the
  palm lean inspectorate · and everyone at the horse latitudes text mode
  compo, where this entry is still in the queue. no hurry
```

Everyone in the greetz is made up. The working notes live in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md); the renderer page is [web/index.html](web/index.html); the reference renderer is [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py).
